reviews.title: Great but one suggestion
reviews.contents:
App is great and works well connected to Apple Health/Garmin Connect. Syncs instantly and insights are good - what I feel dip-wise is mirrored by the app in time as well as productivity times.
The only suggestion I would give, and it is a big one for me as it would determine if I actually subscribe or not, is about work hours. It would be better to include work hours so the suggestions about bed time and relax window are more accurate. As an example, my bed time is determined to be 1am by the app. Unfortunately, I work until 2am and by the time I hit the bed, I’m past my window. The wind down window is around midnight, which is still in the “middle” of my shift and I cannot get any downtime. It does sync with my body clock, so it is accurate, but unfortunately I have to push past this everyday so those windows are not relevant to me. So if there was a way to include those sleep calculations around a shift work, and have an updated estimate of bedtime and wind down window and wake up time, it would be 5 stars for me. Granted, it might not be the direction you want the app to go. But just putting it out there :) Thanks for a great app!

reviews.title: Used to be amazing but now broken
reviews.contents:
I was very impressed by this app when I first got it. It served as great indication of when I might experience a dip in my energy during the day and really helped me focus on my bad sleeping habits. 
However, all this changed with Apple’s most recent iOS update. Since the upgrade to iOS 16 and the addition of the Apple Watch’s ability to track sleep phases, this app has started tracking time awake during the night as time asleep. As someone who wakes up constantly during the night (think probably 10+ times), this severely impacts the accuracy of the measurements and the resulting energy ups and downs during the day. The app also doesn’t calculate any time asleep after my phone’s daily waking alarm (say if you decide to go back to bed for 2 hours after you blindly turn the alarm off) and has never autonomously recognised a nap yet. As a result, the energy level indicators are more of a gimmick at this point, which is really disappointing, considering I felt they were pretty accurate at the beginning. 
It is also somewhat frustrating that you cannot access the various energy level predictions from previous days, but can only see the current day’s predictions. It feels like a missing functionality that should be there for comparison purposes and to track progress. 
I’m disappointed that a subscription based app with so much advertising put into it suddenly is experiencing so many issues and there have been no updates to address them yet.

reviews.title: Not the detail of app I am looking for unfortunately
reviews.contents:
I downloaded this and decided to give it a go using the free trial first - otherwise it is £60 per year - I have used it for two nights via the nightstand method - it tells me I slept as an example 8 1/2 hours last night - shows as this amazing amount of sleep however it did not record that I woke up about seven times - I was awake for around four hours in that 8 1/2 hour period - so I don’t know what the difference is and if you have an Apple Watch, maybe it records all that ?? But I do not have one of those and it tells me using the stand feature that it listens all night and you keep your keep your phone on next to the bed - I was thinking maybe it listens to my breathing and noises et cetera in order to determine even if not completely accurate when I am awake and when I go into a deep sleep - but it has done nothing - just tells me I had a wonderful 8 1/2 hours sleep 🙈 this is not the kind of app I am looking for - so unfortunately I will be cancelling my free trial and removing the app. 

If you are a good sleeper and you just want to keep a record of when you go to sleep and when you wake up - when to stop drinking coffee - and an app to tell you when you might feel groggy - then this app will work for you, but unfortunately for me, I am looking for an app that tells me about my quality of sleep (or lack of) hence the reason why I downloaded it to give it a go in the first place 🥰

reviews.title: Helping you get energy back
reviews.contents:
For the past several years, I always tried to get 8 hours of sleep, but still felt tired. When I started using Rise and tracking my sleep, I found out that it was more like 6.5 hours (noise, light and other factors can cause you to wake up during the night) and I optimally needed 8.5! Rise also showed me that I have a 12+ hour sleep deficit just in the past two weeks alone. Over the past seven days, it has been helping me find the best bedtime by calculating the natural window when the body produces melatonin and showing me the times during the day when I should be most active and when I need to rest. My sleep debt is now half, around 6 hours, and getting smaller every day thanks to this.

I really really recommend it. It's very hard to maintain a balanced daily sleep routine with everything that's going on, but this is an amazing reference and guide, using technology and insightful research to help you slow down and get the rest you need. 

I would suggest setting a smart alarm to get the recommended hours if you can, and every day Rise will let you know when to go to sleep to lower your sleep debt. A huge thank you to the Rise team for putting this tool together, you're making a real difference!!! 😴☁️🧸🌟

reviews.title: Good app, very frustrating to use.
reviews.contents: First off, the app concept is great and all the science seems legit and everything in that aspect checks out. However, the app itself is extremely frustrating and annoying to use. First of all, every time you log out and want to log back in you have to go through the 4 or 5 introductory slides every single time. Now that shouldn’t be an issue for most people because you won’t need to log in and out probably ever. So why did I do it? Well shortly after signing up I saw that the sleep data that the app got from my Apple Health were very inaccurate and so the app was suggesting me ridiculous timings based on that data (which I know isn’t the app’s fault). And so I wanted to delete the Apple Health sleep data and start fresh, but doing so didn’t change anything in the app so then I tried revoking the app’s permission to access Apple Health, that also didn’t do anything. So at this point I thought I’d just delete the account and create a new one, and well there is no option to delete your account. So I log out and try create a new account using another email (after going through the 4-5 slides again), and that brand new account had the same data and settings and habits that I’ve set on the other account. At that point I gave up and just deleted the app. All in all, if you wanna use this app, make sure you check everything’s all good before signing up.

reviews.title: Good but could do with improvements
reviews.contents:
I’ve tried many sleep apps over the years and this one does feel quite unique compared to some of them. It’s helped me to consider energy levels and the fact I may have been trying to go to sleep too early, hence having a more restless sleep. I’m not going to sleep later but sleeping solidly with more energy.
The reason I won’t be subscribing beyond the free week trial is because of the lack of user friendliness. The different sections of app is all over the place and it takes me ages to find what I’m looking for, and then I forget where to find it again the next time I’m looking for it. 
I also didn’t quite understand how you change the suggested sleep time, as it was suggesting quite a late time and a late get up, but because I need to get up early for work, this didn’t fit with my routine. Maybe this would mean having to use the app for longer but I just became a bit impatient with it. 
I rarely leave reviews but with this app I feel like there is so much potential that I wanted to make sure feedback is received so that the improvements can be made, as it’s something I would consider using in the future. There elements I appreciate and have learnt things about my sleep routine, but it also needs to be made more use friendly (and I’m not a tech novice).

reviews.title: This is a scam.
reviews.contents: Sold by the adverts and in hopes of understanding my sleep better I paid for and downloaded the app. I’ve tried it for a month and can confidently say that this is a scam. Gives you absolutely nothing of value. All that the app focuses on is sleep debt. Not based on the quality of your sleep but rather the quantity. I can say this because I connected my garmin watch to the app to feed my sleep data and get better results. But even in the days when my sleep quantity was adequate(8-9 hours) but the quality was extremely poor based on my watch (which is obviously more accurate), the app would only take into account the quantity and tell me I’ve had a great sleep even though I am feeling like a zombie and of course vice versa. Similarly when I downloaded the app I had hoped that the app would let me know my sleep needs but it does not. You have to feed your ideal sleep quantity to the app and based on that it makes all sorts of assumptions. And that is all that it does. I am utterly disappointed. I am essentially a night owl and want to become a morning person, this is the main reason I got the app because that is what the ads suggested but it is a lie. The app does not possess the technology to read sleep data nor the inclination to help people. It apparently is just a money making machine for the developers who have does a fantastic job at marketing.

reviews.title: Great idea, poor UX
reviews.contents:
The idea behind this app is great and I found it really educational and think it has helped me understand more about my sleep patterns. It encourages you to emphasise getting enough sleep and not feel like you're being lazy! I like the interactive graph where you can add sections of not sleeping or add naps. And the design and colour scheme is cool. For that reason I paid for a discounted subscription. 

Sadly the user experience with the app itself is really frustrating. Often on the graph the words overlay each other so you can't read them properly. There are regularly issues with syncing to fitbit and getting accurate data. Once when I couldn't sleep in the night, on the iphone widget for rise there appeared a popup for a guided meditation to help you sleep type thing which I clicked on but could literally never find again (found that actually quite spooky!). Lastly when I switched phones the setup for the app on the new phone was so long and frustrating - no option to just log in! You have to go through the ten page flow to sign up then log out of your new account then log back in to the original one if you want your data. So disappointing for any app let alone a paid one.

reviews.title: ADHD game changer
reviews.contents:
I have been using rise for 1 year and have just renewed my subscription. Although I feel the app is on the pricey side it has been really useful in helping me navigate my recent ADHD diagnosis. The app lets me know how much energy I have, when I will have my highest and lowest energy points in the day so I can plan my day better and by tracking my sleep deficit it allows me to plan and catch up on those missing hours of sleep on my days off. I use RISE alongside another app called Sleepcycle and highly recommend they are used together. RISE can integrate the data from Sleepcycle into its app which is great!

I have recommended RISE to many of my friends and now have 5 of them using the app and loving it! It would be great if there was a referral scheme that offered a discount to current users upon their next renewal. I would also add a new toggle/add on for medication reminders and water reminders if I could. It would be great to set a water drinking goal on the app too as it helps with your sleep if you drink enough water. Brilliant app!

reviews.title: Incredible, highly recommended
reviews.contents:
Hiya,

So I decided to write this after seeing some other reviews because I feel they made an injustice to this app in theirs. This actually cured my insomnia. The fact that it tells me when i should go to sleep helps me force myself to sleep. Plus i can now lie down and sleep when i see that it’s time to do so. I’m not even sure how it cured my insomnia but it did. Ive seen many reviews about bugs and pricing. I accidentally bought this after the trial for a year (£50) and so i forced myself to use it. During the trial i used it every day though so I wasnt too angry (ive used it everyday since too). All the bug claims havent happened to me, the app works fine and has always done so. The addition of an alarm clock would also be a life saver because apple’s is bad.. very. The way it works with the sleep bit in health means i cant make it so i have a lie in on saturdays and sundays. I always have to wake up and its so annoying (plus i think if i turn it off rise cant track my sleep thing in health). anyways its a great app, highly recommended
